note: The journal's web of what needs what (J2a, docs 13, 15). rows: the bands top to bottom, each a list of node ids in left-to-right order; the order is chosen so no two links cross and no link passes behind a name (keep that when adding species). nodes: the label, and what the node stands for: page (a journal page id; the node is a pencil ? until that page is known), flag (a journal flag that makes it known) or always (known from the start, as you are). A name is also known once any of its links is inked. intro: the line under the web before a name is tapped. unknown: how a name not yet seen shows (label), and what tapping it says (line, then hint, which names the known things linked into it so it hints without telling). links: a, b and ink, the trigger that inks the link: grows:<ground>:<plant> (that plant seen growing on that ground; plants on grass-painted ground count as growing in soil), seen:<page> (that page known), mossOnRock (moss seen on painted rock), or flag:<name> (a journal flag, such as frogs:settled, set when frogs arrive in S6). note: the line the journal writes the first time a link inks (links already true when the journal starts ink quietly). textPx: the label size in drawing units (18 reads at 16 px on a 375 px phone). gapPx: the space between names in a row; chipPadPx: the room around a name inside its chip (both sides together); the widest row, with every name known, must stay near 380 units so names read at 16 px on a 375 px phone (a unit test checks); linkGapPx: the wider space between two neighbours linked to each other, so that link reads as a line; rowGap: the space between rows; bandPad: the padding of each band's background.
intro: Ground at the top, plants in the middle, animals below. Inked links are ones you have seen happen; pencil ones you have not, yet. A ? is something you have not met. Tap a name to follow its links.
